subject: Re: Intermittent latency spikes on private deployment — request for SLA addendum
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@bluehorizonlabs.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, rajiv.sinha@bluehorizonlabs.com
Date: Tue, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent latency spikes on private deployment — logs attached

Hi Marcus,

We're seeing recurring tail-latency spikes on our Private deployment in us-west that started late last week. Most calls are fine (p95 ~ 120ms) but we have a small but meaningful number of requests that jump into the 800–1200ms range for short bursts (~3–10 min). Attach is a set of sample traces and token-level timings from Friday and this morning.

What we've tried: restarted our edge NAT, rotated the upstream peering, and temporarily increased our egress capacity — the pattern persists. This is impacting customer-facing inference (chat sessions that time out) and we need to understand whether this is a Redwood serving issue or something in our networking.

Ask: can we get an SLA exception/addendum that explicitly addresses shared-responsibility for customer-managed edge infrastructure while we triage? Specifically, we want clarity about:
- When Redwood will accept attribution of a latency breach versus when the customer's managed edge is excluded.
- A narrow carveout for customer-controlled components, and an interim mitigation plan (monitoring/alerting recommendations).

Attached: bh-latency-sample-20280520.zip (pcap + token-timings.csv)

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call.

Olivia Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Blue Horizon Labs
olivia.park@bluehorizonlabs.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0197

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@bluehorizonlabs.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@naomi_feldman@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 May 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spikes on private deployment — logs attached

Hi Olivia — thanks for the packet captures and timings. Sorry you're seeing this.

Quick plan:
1) Naomi (copied) will triage the traces and confirm whether the tail looks like upstream egress/networking or server-side KV/cache stalls.
2) I will work with Kimberly (legal) for a short-form addendum we can propose that documents a narrowly scoped exclusion for customer-controlled edge components while preserving Redwood's uptime commitments for the managed stack.
3) If needed we can schedule a joint debugging call today or tomorrow — when are you available?

For troubleshooting, can you also send:
- The last 24h of Prometheus summaries from your edge (15m rollups)
- Any NAT gateway config changes in the last 48h
- Confirmation of whether you have active DDoS protection/traffic shaping in front of the VPC

I've attached a short diagnostic-request-template.md to make it easy for your ops team to export the bits we need.

I'll aim to get a proposed exception wording by EOD tomorrow so we can keep this moving.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachment: diagnostic-request-template.md

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, Olivia Park <olivia.park@bluehorizonlabs.com>
Cc: rajiv.sinha@bluehorizonlabs.com
Date: Wed, 21 May 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spikes on private deployment — initial triage

Thanks for the packet captures, Olivia. Quick notes from an initial pass:

- Observed symptom: token-level timings show relatively consistent server-side generation times, but multiple samples include an extra 400–900ms pre-flight delay between the inbound request and when the server actually receives it. That suggests the delay is occurring upstream of our inference runtime.
- Evidence: TCP retransmit bursts and increased SYN->ACK RTTs in the pcap correlate with the high-latency request timestamps.

Likely root causes to investigate on the Blue Horizon side:
- Customer-managed egress NAT appliance intermittently queuing/health checks causing bursts
- Peering/transit provider path flaps during the observed windows

Recommendation for SLA language: rather than a blanket exclusion, propose a narrowly scoped exception that:
- Excludes measured latency attributable to customer-controlled edge devices or third-party transit beyond the VPC egress point (we define attribution via packet captures + server ingress timestamps).
- Requires joint evidence within 10 business days to apply the exclusion to a given incident (packet captures + flow logs + a short Redwood triage report).
- Keeps the core uptime/availability SLOs unchanged for Redwood-managed infra and the inference runtime.

I've drafted a short 'technical justification' document and a proposed exception whitepaper; attaching proposed-exception-wp.docx and a short network-trace-summary.txt. If you agree with the narrow wording, Marcus/Kimberly can convert this into contract language.

Naomi Feldman
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed-exception-wp.docx, network-trace-summary.txt

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@bluehorizonlabs.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spikes on private deployment — proposed addendum

Marcus / Olivia — attaching a draft addendum (redwood-addendum-bh.docx) that mirrors Naomi's technical proposal but frames it in contract language. High-level:

- Scope: Narrow carveout that excludes latency breaches attributable to Customer-controlled edge devices, third-party transit after VPC egress, and customer-managed firewall/NAT appliances.
- Attribution: We require packet captures and server ingress timestamps; both parties have 10 business days to provide evidence for each incident.
- Remediation: If attribution points to Redwood, the normal SLA remediation steps apply. If attribution points to the Customer, Redwood will propose mitigation guidance and can offer a 30-day validation window (optional) where we run additional monitoring but do not apply credits.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the overall approach.
2) If accepted, I'll convert this to an addendum and route it via DocuSign (I've included a draft link below).
3) Marcus — can you confirm whether Sales is comfortable approving the proposed 10-business-day evidence window and the validation window wording?

Olivia — if you want a short call to walk through the wording, I have availability Thu 10:00–11:30 PDT.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-addendum-bh.docx
